Every forward caller then becomes rotation-correct with zero further edits.

survey.spriteImpact: Projection alone repositions the SAME baked sprite; it does not rebake. But because building sprites (sprites.js buildSprites/prism/windows) bake exactly two front faces with fixed lighting and a fixed down-right anchor (ox/oy) for r=0, rotating only the projection would leave every building showing its r=0 faces at a rotated screen position — the lit/front faces would point the wrong way for r=1/2/3. To honor the user's 'buildings show different sides' expectation, spriteFor(city,i) must take cam.r and return one of 4 baked facings (rotate the prism's left/right face assignment, window pattern, and lighting per orientation), quadrupling per-building bake work. The projection-picking site that forces this coupling is the 2x2 anchor block (render.js:447-467): its front-corner selection and awx/awy positioning must agree with whichever facing sprite is chosen, so anchor-corner math and facing selection have to be designed together. Autotile masks (road/wire/shore) also rotate their 4-bit N/E/S/W neighbor bits per cam.r, but that is the autotile subsystem, not projection.
survey.notes: The pure coordinate math is small and clean: put rot()/unrot() in worldX/worldY/screenToTile and ~10 forward call sites + the minimap-inverse + postcard bounds all inherit correctness for free. The genuinely hard, correctness-critical parts are (1) reordering the painter loop (render.js:363) into view-space u+v so occlusion stays back-to-front under all 4 r, and (2) the 2x2 anchor block (render.js:447-467) which entangles front-corner selection, sprite positioning, and rotated-facing sprite choice. Both cache keys (tKey 333, nKey 346) must gain cam.r or stale layers blit after a rotate. cam.r must round-trip through save (v8→v9). Camera pan and all screenToTile consumers need no edits — the design goal is to keep rotation centralized in the transform pair plus the loop/anchor, not scattered across ui.js. Verified: main.js does no direct projection; sim.js only defines the TW/TH/HW/HH constants (sim.js:5). cam is defined once at render.js:4.

sites.where: js/render.js — renderFrame(), main tile loop, lines 362-365 (outer `for s=0..(MAP-1)*2`, inner `for x=max(0,s-MAP+1)..min(MAP-1,s)`, `y=s-x`, `i=y*MAP+x`)
sites.assumes: Screen depth (back-to-front) is monotonic in the raw tile sum x+y, because worldY(x,y)=(x+y)*HH+HH. So `s` IS the screen-depth diagonal, back corner is fixed at tile (0,0), and +x/+y both move a tile toward the viewer. This holds only for orientation 0.
sites.rotationApproach: Parameterize the walk by a rotation R. Keep worldX/worldY fixed and feed them rotated coords (X,Y)=R(x,y) where R maps the logical grid to the four screen orientations (0:(x,y); 90:(y,MAP-1-x); 180:(MAP-1-x,MAP-1-y); 270:(MAP-1-y,x)). The outer loop must then step over ascending projected depth d=X+Y, and the inner loop enumerates the logical tiles whose R-image lands on that diagonal. Simplest concrete form: precompute per rotation the (dxScreen,dyScreen) unit steps and iterate s over X+Y with the analogous y=s-x reconstruction applied to the rotated axes; the back corner becomes (MAX,0)/(MAX,MAX)/(0,MAX) for 90/180/270 respectively. Inner order within one depth band remains free for occlusion (same-depth sprites are side-by-side and never overlap), so only the depth GROUPING must equal projected X+Y — that constraint is what the night flush below depends on.

Trigger: fire when the loop reaches the footprint corner with MAXIMUM projected depth for R — 0:(ax+s-1,ay+s-1); 90:(ax+s-1,ay); 180:(ax,ay); 270:(ax,ay+s-1). Anchor/position: draw at the footprint corner with MINIMUM projected depth (the back corner) for R, i.e. the opposite corner — 0:(ax,ay); 90:(ax,ay+s-1); 180:(ax+s-1,ay+s-1); 270:(ax+s-1,ay). Pair this with a per-facing sprite whose ox/oy is baked relative to that rotation's back corner. survey.spriteImpact: Four facings require baking the two visible front faces per rotation for every building (spriteFor/prism/windows/roof output x4), because the painter loop paints a single sprite per building and only its anchor placement is chosen by rotation — the pixels showing the correct two faces must come from the sprite itself. Critically, MULTI-TILE sprites need per-facing ox/oy: the loop anchors a 2x2 sprite at whichever footprint corner is back-most in screen space (see the anchor site), and that corner is a different physical corner of the bitmap for each of the 4 rotations, so each baked facing must carry its own anchor offset measured from that rotation's back corner. 1x1 sprites (ox/oy at diamond center) are anchor-stable and only need the 4 face variants. Overlay silhouettes reused by the night pass (nightPunch spr) inherit whatever facing the loop draws, so no extra bake there.
survey.notes: The painter loop change is contained and mechanical (reparameterize the diagonal walk by a rotation matrix R feeding fixed worldX/worldY), and three of the subtle sites (night per-diagonal flush, terrain layer, nightPunch/Add positions) become correct for free once the outer loop advances exactly one projected-depth band per step. The genuinely fiddly parts are (1) the 2x2 anchor: the anchor tile stays the logical min-corner but its screen role flips, so BOTH the draw-trigger corner (max projected depth) and the sprite-placement corner (min projected depth) must be selected per rotation and paired with a per-facing ox/oy — easy to get subtly wrong and it manifests as buildings drawn one tile off or z-fighting with the tile in front; and (2) poolBlocked's front-neighbor delta must rotate (1,1)->(1,-1)/(-1,-1)/(-1,1). Inner-loop order within a depth band stays free for occlusion, so no need to reverse the x loop per rotation — only the depth grouping must equal projected X+Y. Cars (render.js:710-713 axis 'x'/'y' body pick) and the autotile neighbor masks are screen-direction/rotation-sensitive too but belong to the sprites/overlay subsystems, not painter-order; flagged only because they share the +x/+y-means-fixed-screen-diagonal assumption. Nothing here touches save format (v8) — painter order is pure presentation, derived from cam + city state each frame.

This keeps every seed reproducible AND lets you choose whether a lit-window pattern is welded to a world-face (same stream per face) or varies per facing. Save v8 is unaffected: orientation is camera/view state, never per-tile serialized, and the (x+2y)&3 jitter pick stays per-tile deterministic.

survey.spriteImpact: Buildings are the cost center. Today ~45 zoned DAY canvases (9 families x NV=5) each fanned to 4 value-jitter copies (~225 day canvases) plus ~14 civic/plant/reward sprites, with night/pool/beacon layers shared by reference and winter derived via makeWinter. Because every prism bakes only the two south faces, rotation cannot be done by transform at draw time — the hidden NW/NE faces and all face-welded content (windows, doors, signs, bay doors, canopies, ridge/door on tinyHouse, back-corner stacks, front-corner pools) simply do not exist in the bake. So the DAY building bakes (and everything derived from them: night, pool, beacon, jitter, and the winter/autumn seasonal sets) must be baked x4, roughly 4x building canvas memory and 4x building bake time. Order-of-magnitude: if the current building spritesheet is ~a few MB of offscreen canvas, expect ~4x that. Terrain, roads, wires, shore, terrEdge, cars, chopper, smoke puffs, disaster glows, night radial sprites do NOT need re-baking — roads/wires/shore/terrEdge become mask-bit rotations (free), and cars stay single-baked if rotation is done as a tile-coord transform ahead of the fixed worldX/worldY projection. Screen-space overlays (cursor, minimap viewport box, flames, tornado/ufo, chopper, dusk tint) are projection-agnostic and unaffected except where they read hard-coded footprint offsets (smoke emit points, poolBlocked front-neighbor).
survey.notes: Core finding: prismFrom() only ever draws the two south-facing screen faces (SW=W->S, SE=S->E) and the top; the N-facing back pair is never baked, so there is no draw-time transform that can reveal 'different sides' on rotation — the other sides must be baked. Keep the screen-side lighting convention (SW darker, SE lighter) FIXED across all 4 facings so the sun stays welded to the screen (SC2K behavior); only the face CONTENT rotates. Cheapest wins: roads/wires/shore/terrEdge/beach need NO re-bake — rotate the 4-bit N/E/S/W neighbor mask (m' = rol(m,orient)) before indexing the existing 16-sprite tables (EDGE table, roadMask/wireMask/shoreMask/beachMask/terrEdgeMask). Cars likely free if rotation is implemented as a tile-coordinate transform BEFORE the fixed worldX=(x-y)*HW / worldY=(x+y)*HH+HH projection (both world axes still map to the two screen diagonals, both baked car bodies still apply). Two subtle render.js couplings that must rotate alongside the sprites: (1) the 2x2 anchor draw-trigger (x===ax+size-1 && y===ay+size-1) and the worldX(ax,ay) back-offset assume the back corner is the anchor; (2) updateSmoke()'s hard-coded plume offsets and poolBlocked()'s (x+1,y+1) front-neighbor check assume the fixed front. Determinism: fork a per-orientation mulberry32 stream (baseSeed ^ orient-salt) or snapshot/restore RNG state per orientation loop — reuse the existing gasRng/shoreRng/forestRng swap idiom — so orientation 0 stays reproducible and you control whether lit-window patterns are welded per world-face or vary per facing. Save v8 is untouched: view orientation is camera state, not serialized per tile. Biggest design decision (not a mechanical port): buildings with a true front (fire bays, hospital ER canopy, school/shop doors) — decide whether they keep a fixed world-front that rotates out of view, or always turn to face the camera; that choice determines whether 4 real facings or effectively 2 mirrored ones are baked.

survey.notes: Most of this subsystem collapses to ONE dependency: make worldX/worldY/screenToTile rotation-aware and the chopper, disasters, smoke puffs, dusk/seasonal screen fills, and all camera-jump navigation become correct automatically. The genuine per-site work is (1) the THREE hidden inline copies of the projection that will silently stay at orientation 0 — car headlight heading (render.js 716-719), minimap camera-rect inverse (1136-1137), and postcardBounds corner-picks (postcard.js 44-45); (2) the car axis->sprite pick flip (711-712); (3) the plume chimney offsets, which are coupled to per-facing building bakes; and (4) the minimap, a policy decision — either rotate it to match the view (then also rotate the camera-rect and click-to-pan inverse) or deliberately leave it north-up. Nothing here needs new sprite art except possibly cars, and even that is optional. drawFlames/flameLayer, dusk tint, seasonal grade, drawNightLayer, and flushCarLights are pure screen-space and need no changes beyond their upstream anchor/heading. The 'district' item in the subsystem brief has no standalone screen-space label renderer in the code (district appears only as minimap G8 dimming context and scenario data); it is effectively the postcard/minimap paths covered above.

architecture.approach: Add ONE field `cam.r ∈ {0,1,2,3}` (90° CCW steps) as the single source of orientation truth, and route all tile↔screen math through the existing worldX/worldY/screenToTile chokepoint plus two new pure integer helpers rot()/unrot() (reflections/swaps about the square map center — MAP is confirmed a single square dimension). Rotation is a per-tile integer coordinate remap applied BEFORE the unchanged iso formula on the forward path and AFTER the inverse on the backward path — never a ctx matrix rotate, never per-pixel. This makes ~90% of the renderer (cars, chopper, disasters, smoke anchors, centerOn, clampCam, cursor footprint, postcard, night glows) correct for free once the three chokepoint functions know r. FIVE sites need real per-r logic beyond inheritance: (1) screenToTile inverse, (2) the painter loop must iterate VIEW-space depth diagonals, (3) the 2x2 anchor trigger/position corners, (4) poolBlocked's front-neighbor delta, (5) autotile mask lookup (a free 4-bit cyclic rotate). BUILDING sprites are the one heavyweight: the bake only exists for the two south faces, so honoring "different sides" requires baking 4 facings, done LAZILY and deterministically. Everything else stays single-baked. Two conflicts resolved decisively: (a) sprite strategy = lazy 4-facing bake as primary with a billboard pref as phase-1/low-memory fallback (not either/or — ship billboard first, facings behind the same projection core); (b) masks = lookup-time rot4 rotation, NOT neighbor re-probing (connectivity is orientation-invariant). Rotation is VIEW-ONLY state (cam is never serialized — confirmed sim.js:1358 serialize has no cam field), so no save-format bump; r persists only in UI.prefs. r=0 output stays byte-identical to HEAD by construction.
architecture.spriteStrategy:
RESOLUTION of the central conflict: bake 4 facings for developed buildings — lazily and deterministically — as the primary design, with a billboard mode as a shipping-first fallback behind the SAME projection core. prismFrom (sprites.js:80-97) welds only the two south world-faces with screen-fixed lighting and face-welded decoration (windows(), doors, bays, storefronts, tinyHouse ridge/door, stacks, groundPool, roof furniture); the NW/NE faces literally do not exist in pixels, so a draw-time transform can reposition but never reveal a different side. Therefore genuine "different sides" requires re-running the bake with the world-front face-pair reselected per r.

Design: KEEP the sun screen-welded across all facings (SW darker via shade(base,.72), SE lighter shade(base,.92) — SC2K convention); ROTATE only WHICH world-face's decoration maps onto the screen SW/SE bottom edges. buildSprites wraps its building-bake body in `for r in 0..3`; each SPR.<fam> becomes SPR.<fam>[r] carrying its own ox/oy (1x1 anchor at diamond center is r-stable; 2x2 ox/oy baked relative to that r's back corner). spriteFor(city,i) gains cam.r and returns SPR.<fam>[cam.r][variant]. Box+window buildings (r2,r3,c2,c3,i2,i3) get a "windows on all four world faces" default so every facing reads populated. The ~10 genuinely handed buildings (fire-station 3 bays + red band, i1 loading door, school double doors, hospital canopy, c1 storefront/awning, police blue band/badge, tinyHouse gable ridge+door for r1/mayor, coal/gas/i2/i3 smokestacks, c3 beacon mast + roof furniture) tag their feature to ONE world face; at the two orientations where that face rotates to an occluded back, the visible pair is simply drawn plainer — this is INTENDED, verify it doesn't read as missing-art.

DETERMINISM (the sharp risk): naive 4x through shared ART_RNG (sprites.js:683) desyncs every downstream sprite and breaks r=0 byte-identity. Fork a per-orientation stream via the existing gasRng/shoreRng snapshot-swap idiom (sprites.js:1290-1308): facing 0 keeps the ORIGINAL seed 0x5EED (byte-identical to HEAD, gated by a pixel-hash regression test); facings 1..3 use `mulberry32(0x5EED ^ (r*0x9E3779B1))`, so bake order is irrelevant. LAZY bake: only facing 0 at boot (boot time + default memory unchanged); facings 1..3 baked on first visit to that r and cached (SPR.<fam> → SPR.<fam>[r] built on demand). Night/pool/beacon/jitter/winter derive per facing as today. Memory grows from a few MB toward ~4x only if the player visits all orientations (~10-16MB, acceptable desktop). Optional dedup: symmetric boxes have facing2≡0, facing3≡1 → alias to cut to 2 unique bakes; implement only if measured high. Billboard fallback (a pref): spriteFor always returns facing 0 regardless of cam.r — projection still repositions correctly, city reads fine, zero extra bake — ship as phase-1, promote to facings as phase-2. Projection/painter core is identical either way. NOT rebaked: roads/wires/shore/beach/terrEdge (mask rotation), terrain diamonds, cars, chopper, smoke puffs, disaster/night radial glows, cursor, minimap.
architecture.picking: screenToTile is the single picking chokepoint (render.js:226). Its fix (recover float view u,v → round in view space → unrot) makes ALL consumers correct with zero edits: ui.js hover:378, tap:427, paint:458, applyToolAt:489, and ambience.js:22. drawCursor's footprint loop (render.js:1032-1049) needs NO change — it draws worldX(x+dx,y+dy) over the axis-aligned tile footprint and each diamond projects correctly once worldX is rotation-aware; the hover anchor already comes from rotation-aware screenToTile, so multi-tile placement previews on the intended footprint at every r. canPlace/cost are tile-space and orientation-invariant; anc stays the logical min-corner. The one verification item: round u,v in VIEW space BEFORE unrot so "nearest tile under cursor" stays the visually-nearest diamond near diagonal boundaries. The minimap click-to-pan (ui.js:566-571) stays correct with no inverse-rotation because the minimap grid stays north-up (see overlays) — it maps pixel→tile→cam via rotation-aware worldX/worldY.
architecture.overlays:
Most overlays inherit correctness from rotation-aware worldX/worldY/screenToTile. The exceptions:

Cars (render.js:710-719): keep TWO baked iso bodies (projection only ever yields two screen diagonals). Axis→sprite pick must consult r — rotate the tile travel delta first: `const {u,v}=rot(c.tx,c.ty,cam.r), {u:u0,v:v0}=rot(c.fx,c.fy,cam.r); axis = (u-u0)!==0?'x':'y'` (effectively swaps on odd r). The headlight vector (render.js:716-719) INLINES the r=0 projection (rx=(tdx-tdy)*HW, ry=(tdx+tdy)*HH) — a hidden second transform that will NOT follow worldX/worldY; replace with the rotated delta: du=u-u0, dv=v-v0; rx=(du-dv)*HW, ry=(du+dv)*HH. flushCarLights (731-758) is pure screen-space downstream — no change.

Smoke (render.js:791-800): plume spawns use hard-coded screen deltas (coal -18/HH-78, gas -14/HH-62, ZI -12/-68) assuming the stack sits back-left at r=0. In 4-facing mode the stack re-bakes to the rotated back corner, so store a per-facing baked emit-anchor {dx,dy} on each building sprite and read it in updateSmoke. In billboard fallback, leave offsets fixed. Fire smoke (787-789) is symmetric — no change.

poolBlocked (render.js:195-204): the screen-nearer occluder is the tile whose VIEW image is at (u+1,v+1); derive the map-space delta from unrot's linear part — r0:(+1,+1) r1:(+1,-1) r2:(-1,-1) r3:(-1,+1). Compute delta from cam.r (from the SAME unrot so it can't drift), bounds-check, sample.

Chopper (883-963), tornado/ufo (965-1030), night radial glows (568-583): vertically/radially symmetric, built in screen space around the tile's projected (wx,wy) — correct for free once the anchor tile is rotation-aware. Optional cosmetic: chopper launch picks nearest SCREEN edge post-rotation — low priority.

Minimap (render.js:1085-1149): RESOLUTION — keep north-up/orthographic (resolve against the rotate-the-grid idea; a stable overview is better UX and keeps the click handler trivial). The grid loop needs no change. Only the viewport rect (1131-1149) must route its four screen corners through the shared screenToTile instead of the inline r=0 inverse, so the box becomes the rotated visible region's tile-space bbox — an acceptable indicator. ui.js minimap click (566-571) stays correct since the grid stays north-up.

Postcard (postcard.js:44-45): project ALL FOUR map-bbox corners through rotation-aware worldX/worldY and take min/max for x0/x1/y0/y1 (don't assume which corner is extreme — they swap at r=1/3). renderPhotoTo (render.js:537-548) must save/restore cam.r alongside cam.x/y/z and render the photo at an EXPLICIT r=0 for stable framing, then restore — never leak live r.
architecture.uiAnimation:
Control: bind Q = rotate CCW, E = rotate CW, with `[` / `]` as aliases (all four key slots are free — TOOLS uses 0-9, -, =, +, w,s,h,g,i,m,b), plus two HUD buttons (⟲/⟳) near the minimap. Intercept in the keydown listener (ui.js:514) BEFORE the `TOOLS.find(e.key)` lookup (ui.js:528) so a rotate key never falls through to tool selection. rotateView(dir): capture the tile under screen-center via screenToTile(cvs.width/2, cvs.height/2) FIRST; set `cam.r=(cam.r+dir+4)&3`; then PIVOT IN PLACE — cam.x=worldX(c.x,c.y), cam.y=worldY(c.x,c.y) (now rotation-aware) so the view spins around what the player is looking at instead of jumping; clampCam(); UI.prefs.viewRot=cam.r; savePrefs(). On first rotation to an un-baked facing, kick the lazy per-orientation bake (one-time ~few-hundred-ms hitch; optionally pre-bake all 4 in an idle callback after boot as a pref).

Snap vs animated: SNAP by default — the iso projection is discrete (4 baked facings, 4 mask rotations); there is no cheap way to render intermediate angles without a real affine ctx transform, which breaks pixel-snapped sprite alignment and determinism. Do NOT interpolate tile positions. Optional polish: a short ~180ms purely-presentational turn done as a screen-space ctx.rotate of the PREVIOUS frame's snapshot bitmap easing out while the new orientation renders in — never touches sim state, fully skippable. Respect motion prefs: `matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches` (or UI.prefs.reduceMotion) → snap instantly. Debounce so held keys don't queue more than one turn per animation. Add a one-line entry to the F1 shortcuts overlay.
architecture.saveImpact: VIEW-ONLY, NOT serialized — this overrides the survey's "bump v8→v9" suggestion, and view-only is the correct call. Confirmed in code: cam.x/cam.y/cam.z are render-module globals, NOT part of city.serialize() (sim.js:1358 has no cam field), reset on newCity (ui.js:1244 `cam.x=0; cam.y=MAP*HH; cam.z=1`) and merely clampCam'd on loadCity (ui.js:1231). cam.r belongs to the same ephemeral view state, so: NO save-format change, NO v8→v9 bump, older saves round-trip untouched. Nothing per-tile is orientation-dependent — anc stays the logical min-corner, varnt/lvl are orientation-free, and the (x+2y)&3 jitter pick stays tile-space deterministic, so serialize() stays deterministic and portable. Recommendation: initialize cam.r:0 in the cam literal (render.js:4); add `cam.r=0` to the newCity reset line (ui.js:1244). For "resume at last orientation," persist r in the SEPARATE UI.prefs localStorage blob (PREFS_KEY 'simcity99.prefs', alongside dayNight/autoBudget) via savePrefs(), and on boot init `cam.r=(UI.prefs.viewRot|0)&3` (default 0) — a per-player display preference that survives reload but is NOT baked into a shared/exported city (the correct semantics: a shared save must not force the recipient's camera angle). Never put r in the city save.
architecture.risks:
Turn-direction handedness (biggest risk): THREE places encode "which way is 90°" — rot()/unrot(), rot4() mask cycling, and poolBlocked's front-neighbor delta. They MUST agree. Mitigation: derive mask direction and the poolBlocked delta FROM rot()/unrot() (compute front delta as unrot(u+1,v+1,r) − unrot(u,v,r)), never hand-code a second table; verify rot4's rol/ror against one empirical 90° turn where a road tee and a building rotate the same visual way. Fix once, then frozen.

Determinism/regression: r=0 must stay byte-identical to HEAD. Guard by rot(x,y,0) early-returning {u:x,v:y} (no arithmetic) and rot4(m,0)=m. The 4x building bake risks desyncing shared ART_RNG and shifting even r=0 sprites — mitigate with the forked per-orientation stream (facing 0 keeps seed 0x5EED), gated by a pixel-hash regression test on the r=0 spritesheet.

Perf/memory: rotation adds one branch + ≤2 subtractions per projected tile — negligible. Real cost is 4x building canvas memory/bake — mitigate with lazy per-orientation bake (boot unchanged), optional symmetric-building dedup, and the billboard fallback pref if memory-constrained. Cache keys: forgetting cam.r in tKey (render.js:333) or nKey (346) blits a stale pre-rotation layer — append cam.r to both (one line each, must-do); a rotation then costs exactly ONE terrain+night rebuild, matching pan/zoom discipline.

Regression surface — hidden inline projections: the two second-copies (car headlight render.js:716-719, minimap viewport inverse 1131-1140) plus smoke offsets (791) and postcard corners (postcard.js:44) will silently stay r=0 if left. Mitigation: route all through the shared helpers; grep for `*HW`/`*HH` and `/HW`/`/HH` OUTSIDE worldX/worldY/screenToTile to catch any other inlined projection.

Edge cases: (1) picking rounds in VIEW space before unrot, else diagonal-seam tiles mispick; (2) 2x2 anchor trigger=argmax / position=argmin of view-depth, not hard-coded — a wrong corner draws the building a tile off or double-draws; the trigger tile is always in-footprint so in-map even at edges; (3) rot4 straights 5↔10 stay straight and a T connects to the visually-touching edge — assert; (4) poolBlocked delta sign per r or lobby glow bleeds through the wrong face; (5) directional buildings correctly show a plainer BACK at the 2 orientations where their handed feature is occluded — intended, verify it doesn't read as a bug; (6) smoke emit tracks the re-baked stack per facing or plumes float off the chimney; (7) clampCam/postcard bounds — a square map's iso outline is the same diamond at every 90° turn so world extents are unchanged, but verify postcardBounds min/max over all 4 corners frames correctly at r=1/3 where extreme corners swap; (8) rot() assumes NxN (MAP confirmed square) — if maps ever become rectangular, rot must take separate W/H.

criteria.statement: cam.r is the single orientation source: it exists on the cam global, is always an integer in {0,1,2,3}, and the rotate op cam.r=(cam.r+dir+4)&3 cycles through all four values and returns to start after 4 CW or 4 CCW steps. No other module holds a competing orientation variable.
criteria.check: Headless: assert typeof cam.r==='number' && cam.r in {0,1,2,3}; call rotateView(+1) x4 and rotateView(-1) x4, assert cam.r returns to its start each cycle. grep confirms no second orientation global.

criteria.statement: rot() and unrot() are exact integer inverses for every tile at every orientation, including the N-1 boundary row/column: unrot(rot(x,y,r),r) === {x,y} and rot(unrot(u,v,r),r) === {u,v} for all x,y,u,v in 0..MAP-1 and all r in 0..3. rot(x,y,0) returns {u:x,v:y} with no arithmetic; rot4(m,0)===m.
criteria.check: Headless double loop over all MAP*MAP tiles x 4 r asserting round-trip equality; static/AST check that the r===0 branch is an identity early-return.

criteria.statement: Orientation-0 is byte-identical to HEAD by construction: worldX(x,y), worldY(x,y) and screenToTile(sx,sy) return numerically identical results to the HEAD baseline for all tiles when cam.r===0, and the full frame render at r=0 matches a HEAD canvas snapshot.
criteria.check: Compare worldX/worldY over all tiles and screenToTile over a grid of screen points against values captured from HEAD; pixel-diff a headless canvas render at r=0 against a HEAD render of the same seed/camera (zero differing pixels).

criteria.statement: The facing-0 building spritesheet is pixel-identical to HEAD: forking the per-orientation ART_RNG stream (facing 0 keeps seed 0x5EED) leaves every SPR.<fam> facing-0 canvas unchanged, so the 4x bake does not desync shared randomness.
criteria.check: Hash every SPR building canvas at facing 0 after buildSprites() and compare the hash set to a HEAD baseline hash set; assert equal.

criteria.statement: Picking round-trips at every orientation: for each map tile, projecting its center through worldX/worldY and feeding that screen point back through screenToTile returns the same logical (x,y), at all 4 r; rounding happens in view space before unrot so no diagonal-seam mispick occurs.
criteria.check: Headless loop over all tiles x 4 r: p=(worldX,worldY) of tile center in screen coords via the projection+cam transform, assert screenToTile(p)===(x,y). Include tiles adjacent to the map diagonal.

criteria.statement: Painter order stays strictly back-to-front at every orientation: iterating the view-depth diagonals (s=u+v) yields draw calls whose projected screen worldY is monotonically non-decreasing across bands, so no front tile is overdrawn by a back tile at r=1/2/3.
criteria.check: Headless: instrument the painter loop to record worldY per emitted tile in draw order; assert the per-band max worldY is non-decreasing across s for each r.

criteria.statement: Autotile masks rotate at lookup time only: rot4(m,r) is a 4-bit cyclic rotation agreeing in direction with rot()/unrot(); every rotated index is 0..15 and hits an already-baked sprite; straights are preserved (rot4(5,r) and rot4(10,r) stay in {5,10}); the underlying roadMask/wireMask/shore/beach/terrEdge probes are unchanged (connectivity is orientation-invariant).
criteria.check: Enumerate rot4(m,r) for all m,r: assert result in 0..15, assert {5,10} closed under rotation, assert SPR.road[rot4(...)] etc. is defined; assert mask-probe functions are textually unchanged vs HEAD; derive the turn direction from unrot's linear part and assert rot4 matches it.

criteria.statement: 2x2 anchored buildings draw exactly once and in the right cell at every orientation: the draw triggers on the argmax-view-depth footprint corner (always in-footprint, in-map even at edges) and positions from the argmin-view-depth corner, so no double-draw or one-tile offset occurs at any r.
criteria.check: Headless: for a seeded city with 2x2 buildings, instrument anchor emission and assert each 2x2 building emits exactly one draw per frame at each r, and the emitted awx/awy equals worldX/worldY of the argmin-depth corner.

criteria.statement: Rotation invalidates cached layers correctly and cheaply: tKey and nKey both include cam.r, so a single rotation forces exactly one terrain+night rebuild (never a stale pre-rotation blit and never more than pan/zoom would cost); the two inline projections (car headlight render.js:717, minimap viewport inverse render.js:1136) route through the rotation-aware helpers rather than the r=0 formula.
criteria.check: Assert the tKey/nKey strings contain cam.r; toggle cam.r and assert terrLayer/nightLayer rebuild count increments by exactly 1; grep that no *HW//HH inline projection remains outside worldX/worldY/screenToTile except the tile-local diamond-outline draws (429,1045) which operate on an already-projected center.

criteria.statement: Rotation is view-only and never enters the save: city.serialize() output is byte-identical regardless of cam.r, cam.r appears nowhere in the serialized city, old saves load unchanged, and r persists solely in the UI.prefs localStorage blob (initialized cam.r=(UI.prefs.viewRot|0)&3 on boot, reset to 0 on newCity).
criteria.check: Serialize the same city at r=0,1,2,3 and assert identical bytes; grep serialize()/save path for any cam field (expect none); load a HEAD-era save and assert success; assert savePrefs writes viewRot and boot reads it.

risks: Turn-direction handedness is the single highest risk: three sites encode 'which way is 90 degrees' — rot()/unrot(), rot4() mask cycling, and poolBlocked's front-neighbor delta. If they disagree, masks rotate one way and buildings the other. Mitigation: derive the mask direction and the poolBlocked delta FROM rot()/unrot() (front delta = unrot(u+1,v+1,r) - unrot(u,v,r)), never a hand-coded second table; pin rol-vs-ror empirically once in M32a with a road-tee-plus-building visual check, then freeze.

ART_RNG desync from the 4x building bake can silently shift even the r=0 facing-0 sprites, breaking byte-identity. Mitigation: forked per-orientation stream (facing 0 keeps 0x5EED), gated by the C4 spritesheet-hash regression test that must run in CI on every M32b change.
Forgetting cam.r in tKey/nKey (render.js:333/346) blits a stale pre-rotation terrain/night layer — a visually severe, easy-to-miss bug. Must-do one-liner, covered by C9.

Hidden inline projections that stay r=0: the car headlight (render.js:717) and minimap viewport inverse (render.js:1136) plus smoke screen-offsets (render.js:~791) and postcard corners (postcard.js:44) do not inherit worldX/worldY. If left, they silently desync at r!=0. Mitigation: grep for *HW//HH outside the three chokepoints and route all through the helpers.

Picking that rounds logical x,y AFTER unrot instead of rounding u,v in view space BEFORE unrot mispicks tiles along the map diagonal seam — subtle and only visible near boundaries. Covered by C5 with seam-adjacent tiles.

Memory: full 4x building canvas bake if a player visits all orientations (~10-16MB). Mitigation: lazy per-orientation bake keeps boot memory unchanged; optional symmetric-box dedup and the billboard pref as escape hatches.

Directional buildings (fire station, hospital, etc.) correctly render a plainer back face at the 2 orientations where their handed feature is occluded — intended, but risks reading as missing/broken art. Needs a human visual sign-off in M32b, not just a headless check.
plan.recommendation: Ship in the staged order M32a -> M32b -> M32c, and treat M32a as independently releasable. M32a delivers real, usable view rotation (correct projection, picking, masks, overlays, controls) with buildings in billboard mode, and — critically — it is the milestone where the r=0 byte-identity guarantee is established and gated. Make the C2 (rot/unrot inverse), C3 (r=0 projection + full-frame diff), and C4 (spritesheet hash) tests hard merge gates before anything lands, and freeze the handedness convention empirically inside M32a before M32b is written, because M32b's per-facing decoration must rotate the same visual way as the masks — deriving the mask/pool deltas from rot()/unrot() rather than a second table is the way to keep them locked. M32b is the only heavyweight and the only place r=0 byte-identity is at risk again (via ART_RNG), so keep the forked-stream + hash gate running on every M32b commit; its lazy bake means it cannot regress boot time or default memory. M32c is pure polish and can slip without blocking the feature. Go — the architecture is sound: MAP is confirmed square so the NxN rot/unrot holds, the save is confirmed view-only so there is no format bump, and routing everything through the existing worldX/worldY/screenToTile chokepoint plus the two named inline-projection fixes is the correct minimal-surface approach.
